maya-support: Heads up — Acme POC seeing SSE stream drop mid-response when switching from office WiFi -> mobile cellular. Happens consistently when the network swap occurs during an active generation (streaming).

maya-support: Customer report: client shows truncated JSON body (last chunk partial), UI stuck waiting. Browser devtools shows status 0 / 'net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET' sometimes. Server logs show a worker 'write: broken pipe' and our ingress logged HTTP/1.1 499 for the request id. Request id: r-0f3b9a. Model: redwood/gpt-large-v1 (stream).

maya-support: Repro steps they used: mobile webview + our JS SDK v0.7.1. Token rotation enabled (token TTL 60s). Steps: 1) start streaming generation, 2) toggle WiFi off so phone switches to LTE, 3) stream stops ~10-15s after swap. They can repro on iPhone 13, Android Pixel 6.

maya-support: Relevant snippet from server stderr:
```
worker=12 trace: stream.write chunk failed: write: broken pipe
ingress: request_id=r-0f3b9a remote_addr=100.64.12.34 proto=HTTP/1.1 status=499 duration_ms=22112
```

samir-eng: Thanks, Maya. Quick questions: are they using our SDK's built-in reconnect logic or raw fetch()? Any proxy/enterprise VPN in the path? Also does the client show a receive event like `onerror` or just disconnect?

maya-support: They report using SDK's default stream client (no custom reconnect handlers). No corporate VPN, plain mobile carrier NAT. Client sees `onerror` then `onclose`, no explicit retry.

alex-qa: My hypothesis: NAT rebind + IP change means TCP connection gets silently dropped at carrier/proxy. The client token rotation TTL=60s could interact if a new token is requested on reconnect and the old connection is torn in the middle. Two quick repros we should try: (A) force IP flip in lab modem and run `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream"` to see if server emits EOF or partial chunk; (B) disable token rotation on client and rerun.

alex-qa: Example curl to reproduce from a device emu (replace URL):
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <placeholder>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood/gpt-large-v1"
```

samir-eng: On the server side, `write: broken pipe` is consistent with socket close by peer during our write. Two mitigation items we can try: 1) send lighter chunks (reduce server-side chunk size / flush frequency) so partial JSON is less likely to be invalid, 2) add a short heartbeat comment every 5s in SSE (":" comment) to keep NAT state. I'll instrument the worker to log last_event_id and remote IP at disconnect to confirm NAT rebind.

ian-cs: Customer also flagged billing — they saw a full charge for the job even though UI never completed. Can we confirm how we bill aborted/499 streams? Maya, can you pull the billing trace for r-0f3b9a?

maya-support: On it. Preliminary check: billing shows tokens consumed up to the last full chunk we wrote. Need to confirm whether partial trailing chunk counts — will follow up with finance.

samir-eng: Small tweak suggestion for support to try before prod changes: ask customer to enable SDK reconnect+resume (client-side) or retry on `onerror`, and to try disabling token rotation during the test. If that reduces failures, it's likely NAT/connection rebind timing + token exchange race.

deploy-bot: No runtime config or kernel changes deployed in the last 48h to serving runtime in region us-west-2 :white_check_mark:

maya-support: I'll send step-by-step repro to customer: 1) run curl test (alex's command), 2) reproduce with token rotation off, 3) attach HAR / pcap if possible, 4) note exact mobile carrier. Also asking them to try enabling SDK reconnect.

samir-eng: I'll add extra disconnect logging and a temporary heartbeat flag on a staging stream runtime so we can reproduce in-house with modem IP flip. Assigning to me to triage and follow up by EOD. :+1:

maya-support: Thanks — will loop customer in and update thread with billing trace when I have it.
